source.text: דְּבַר־יְהוָ֣ה׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֗ה אֶל־צְפַנְיָה֙ בֶּן־כּוּשִׁ֣י בֶן־גְּדַלְיָ֔ה בֶּן־אֲמַרְיָ֖ה בֶּן־חִזְקִיָּ֑ה בִּימֵ֛י יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בֶן־אָמ֖וֹן מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The word of Yahweh which came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in [the] days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s word came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, during the reign of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
en.R: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave to Zephaniah son of Cushi. His family line went back through Gedaliah and Amariah to Hezekiah. The message came while Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah.

fr.L: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} qui fut adressée à Sophonie fils de Koushi, fils de Guedalia, fils d’Amaria, fils d’Ézéchias, aux jours de Josias fils d’Amon, roi de Juda.
fr.B: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Sophonie fils de Koushi, fils de Guedalia, fils d’Amaria, fils d’Ézéchias, sous le règne de Josias fils d’Amon, roi de Juda.
fr.R: Voici le message que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné à Sophonie fils de Koushi. Sa famille remontait, par Guedalia et Amaria, jusqu’à Ézéchias. Ce message lui a été donné quand Josias fils d’Amon était roi de Juda.

es.L: Palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que vino a Sofonías hijo de Cusí, hijo de Gedalías, hijo de Amarías, hijo de Ezequías, en los días de Josías hijo de Amón, rey de Judá.
es.B: Este mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a Sofonías hijo de Cusí, hijo de Gedalías, hijo de Amarías, hijo de Ezequías, durante el reinado de Josías hijo de Amón, rey de Judá.
es.R: Este es el mensaje que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Sofonías hijo de Cusí. Su familia venía de Gedalías y Amarías, y llegaba hasta Ezequías. El mensaje vino cuando Josías hijo de Amón era rey de Judá.

sw.L: Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lililomjia Sefania mwana wa Kushi, mwana wa Gedalia, mwana wa Amaria, mwana wa Hezekia, katika siku za Yosia mwana wa Amoni, mfalme wa Yuda.
sw.B: Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimjia Sefania mwana wa Kushi, mwana wa Gedalia, mwana wa Amaria, mwana wa Hezekia, wakati wa utawala wa Yosia mwana wa Amoni, mfalme wa Yuda.
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa Sefania mwana wa Kushi. Ukoo wake ulirudi nyuma kupitia Gedalia na Amaria hadi Hezekia. Ujumbe huu ulimjia wakati Yosia mwana wa Amoni alipokuwa mfalme wa Yuda.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah: the heading of the whole book
decisions.reason: The same heading opens Hosea, Joel and Micah. It presents all that follows, the warnings to Judah, the oracles against the nations and the promises of chapter 3, as one message from the LORD, given through a particular man at a particular time. The heading is prose; the poems begin in verse 2. |

decisions.choice: in the days of Josiah: Zephaniah spoke during Josiah's reign over Judah, about 640-609 BC
decisions.reason: Josiah came to the throne as a boy after the murder of his father Amon (2 Kings 21:23-22:1). In his eighteenth year, about 622 BC, he purged the temple and the land of the worship of Baal, the host of heaven and the idol priests (2 Kings 23:4-14). The practices Zephaniah condemns in 1:4-6 are the ones that purge removed, so many date his preaching before it or early in it. The heading itself gives no year. |

decisions.choice: a family line of four generations, back to Hezekiah
decisions.reason: Prophets are usually named with their father only. Zephaniah's line is traced back four generations, perhaps because the last name is that of King Hezekiah of Judah (about 715-686 BC), which would make the prophet a distant member of the royal family. The text does not call this Hezekiah king, so the identification cannot be certain. His father's name, Cushi, can also mean "the Cushite", but here it is a personal name, as in Jeremiah 36:14.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD which came to (L); The LORD's word came to (B); in the days of (L), during the reign of (B), while ... was king (R)
decisions.reason: The heading follows the wording set for the Twelve and published in Hosea 1:1 and Joel 1:1, which follows the Jeremiah table for dated headings. Readable splits the long heading into three sentences and gives the generations as a family line, without adding anything to them. |

decisions.choice: "La parole du SEIGNEUR qui fut adressée à …, aux jours de …" (L); "La parole du SEIGNEUR fut adressée à …, sous le règne de …" (B); "Voici le message que le SEIGNEUR a donné à …, quand … était roi" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's heading formula for the Twelve, as Jeremiah 1:1-2; names as the term sheet: Sophonie, Koushi, Guedalia, Amaria, Ézéchias, Josias fils d'Amon.

decisions.choice: "Palabra del SEÑOR que vino a" (L), "Este mensaje del SEÑOR vino a" (B), "Este es el mensaje que el SEÑOR le dio a" (R); "en los días de" (L), "durante el reinado de" (B), "cuando ... era rey" (R)
decisions.reason: The headings of the Twelve follow the Spanish of Jeremiah 1:1-2 at each level. Sofonías, Cusí, Gedalías, Amarías, Ezequías and Josías hijo de Amón are the published forms.

decisions.choice: "Neno la BWANA lililomjia" (L); "Neno la BWANA lilimjia" (B); "Huu ndio ujumbe ambao BWANA alimpa" (R)
decisions.reason: The book heading follows Jeremiah 1:1-2 and the Hosea and Micah headings, as the term sheet sets. Zephaniah is "Sefania mwana wa Kushi"; Cushi is a man's name here, not the land of Cush.

source.text: אָסֹ֨ף אָסֵ֜ף כֹּ֗ל מֵעַ֛ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Utterly I will sweep away everything from upon [the] face of the ground, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: I will utterly sweep away everything from the face of the ground, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will sweep away everything, all that is on the face of the earth, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will completely sweep away everything on the earth, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Je balaierai entièrement tout de la surface du sol, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Je balaierai tout, tout ce qui est sur la face de la terre, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Je vais complètement balayer tout ce qui est sur la terre, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

es.L: Barreré por completo todo de sobre la faz de la tierra, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Barreré todo, todo lo que hay sobre la faz de la tierra, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Barreré por completo todo lo que hay en la tierra, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nitafagilia mbali kabisa kila kitu kutoka juu ya uso wa ardhi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Nitafagilia mbali kila kitu, vyote vilivyo juu ya uso wa dunia, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Nitafagilia mbali kabisa kila kitu kilicho duniani, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: I will utterly sweep away: I will gather up and remove completely
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubles the verb for emphasis, as if to say "I will sweep, sweep away". The two forms come from verbs that sound alike, one meaning "gather up, take away" and the other "come to an end", so the line also sounds like "I will make an end". The same verb is used for a harvest gathered in; here everything is gathered up to be removed. |

decisions.choice: the face of the ground: the whole surface of the earth where people and animals live
decisions.reason: The word for "ground" is the soil that humans are made from and farm. With the list of people, animals, birds and fish that follows (verse 3), the judgment here reaches all living things, as in the flood (Genesis 6:7). From verse 4 on it narrows to Judah and Jerusalem. |

decisions.choice: utterly sweep away (L); sweep away everything, all that is (B); completely sweep away (R); ground (L), earth (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "ground" for the Hebrew word and gives the doubled verb as "utterly". Balanced repeats "everything ... all that is" to give some of the doubled verb's force, and Balanced and Readable say "earth" because the whole world is meant (m2). |

decisions.choice: *neʾum YHWH* "déclare le SEIGNEUR" (L, B), "dit le SEIGNEUR" (R), for the whole of Zephaniah, Haggai and Zechariah
decisions.reason: The prophets' French formula, as 2 Kings 19:33 and Isaiah.

decisions.choice: "declara" (L), "afirma" (B), "dice" (R) el SEÑOR
decisions.reason: Ne'um YHWH follows the Spanish prophets at each level, always after a comma, through Zephaniah, Haggai and Zechariah.

decisions.choice: "asema BWANA" (L, B); "anasema BWANA" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula ne'um YHWH, as 2 Kings 19:33 and the Isaiah and Jeremiah blocks. Recorded once for this job.

source.text: אָסֵ֨ף אָדָ֜ם וּבְהֵמָ֗ה אָסֵ֤ף עוֹף־הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וּדְגֵ֣י הַיָּ֔ם וְהַמַּכְשֵׁל֖וֹת אֶת־הָרְשָׁעִ֑ים וְהִכְרַתִּ֣י אֶת־הָאָדָ֗ם מֵעַ֛ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: I will sweep away man and beast; I will sweep away [the] birds of the heavens and [the] fish of the sea, and the stumbling blocks with the wicked; and I will cut off humankind from upon [the] face of the ground, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: I will sweep away human and beast; I will sweep away the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, \q and the stumbling blocks with the wicked; \q and I will cut off humankind from the face of the ground, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will sweep away people and animals; I will sweep away the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, \q and the idols that make people fall, together with the wicked. \q I will cut off humankind from the face of the earth, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will sweep away people and animals, the birds in the sky and the fish in the sea. \q I will destroy the wicked and the idols that lead them into sin. \q I will wipe out the human race from the earth, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Je balaierai l’être humain et la bête ; je balaierai les oiseaux des cieux et les poissons de la mer, \q et les occasions de chute avec les méchants ; \q et je retrancherai l’humanité de la surface du sol, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Je balaierai les humains et les bêtes ; je balaierai les oiseaux du ciel et les poissons de la mer, \q et les idoles qui font trébucher les gens, avec les méchants. \q Je retrancherai l’humanité de la surface de la terre, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Je vais balayer les gens et les animaux, les oiseaux du ciel et les poissons de la mer. \q Je vais détruire les méchants et les idoles qui les font tomber dans le péché. \q Je vais faire disparaître le genre humain de la terre, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

es.L: Barreré a hombres y bestias; barreré las aves de los cielos y los peces del mar, \q y los tropiezos junto con los impíos; \q y exterminaré a la humanidad de sobre la faz de la tierra, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Barreré a las personas y a los animales; barreré las aves del cielo y los peces del mar, \q y los ídolos que hacen caer a la gente, junto con los malvados. \q Exterminaré a la humanidad de la faz de la tierra, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Barreré a las personas y a los animales, a las aves del cielo y a los peces del mar. \q Destruiré a los malvados y a los ídolos que los llevan a pecar. \q Borraré de la tierra a la raza humana, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nitawafagilia mbali mwanadamu na mnyama; nitawafagilia mbali ndege wa angani na samaki wa baharini, \q na vikwazo pamoja na waovu; \q nami nitamkatilia mbali mwanadamu kutoka juu ya uso wa ardhi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Nitawafagilia mbali watu na wanyama; nitawafagilia mbali ndege wa angani na samaki wa baharini, \q na sanamu zinazowaangusha watu, pamoja na waovu. \q Nitawakatilia mbali wanadamu kutoka juu ya uso wa dunia, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Nitawafagilia mbali watu na wanyama, ndege wa angani na samaki wa baharini. \q Nitawaangamiza waovu na sanamu zinazowaongoza katika dhambi. \q Nitaiondoa jamii ya wanadamu duniani, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: humans, animals, birds and fish: creation undone
decisions.reason: The list names the living things of Genesis 1 in the reverse of the order in which they were made: humans and animals (day six), then birds and fish (day five). Like the flood (Genesis 6:7, which also speaks of "the face of the ground"), the judgment unmakes what God made. The poem uses the picture to show how complete the judgment will be. |

decisions.choice: the stumbling blocks with the wicked: the idols that make people fall, together with those who worship them
alternatives: the ruins, together with the wicked
a later note added to the text
decisions.reason: The phrase is hard. The word means something that makes people stumble; in Ezekiel 14:3-7 it is used for idols, which cause Israel to fall into sin, and that is the sense taken here. A related word means "ruin" (Isaiah 3:6), so some read "the ruins". The Greek translation is generally said not to have the phrase, and some think it was added as a comment on the verse.

decisions.choice: humankind ... the ground: a play on two related words
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words for "human beings" (adam) and "ground" (adamah) sound alike, recalling that the first human was formed from the ground (Genesis 2:7). The one taken from the ground is cut off from it. |

decisions.choice: the idols that make people fall (B); the idols that lead them into sin (R); stumbling blocks (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "stumbling blocks". Balanced and Readable say what the stumbling blocks are taken to be (m2); the footnote gives the other reading. "Humankind" (L, B) and "the human race" (R) already include men and women.

decisions.choice: "hombres"
decisions.reason: At L "hombres y bestias" names people as a kind, beside the animals; Spanish "hombres" here includes women, so no gender span is needed.

source.text: וְנָטִ֤יתִי יָדִי֙ עַל־יְהוּדָ֔ה וְעַ֖ל כָּל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֞י מִן־הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֶת־שְׁאָ֣ר הַבַּ֔עַל אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם הַכְּמָרִ֖ים עִם־הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal, the name of the idol-priests with the priests,

en.L: And I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against Judah \q and against everyone who dwells in Jerusalem; \q and I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal, \q the name of the idol-priests with the priests,
en.B: I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against Judah \q and against everyone who lives in Jerusalem. \q From this place I will cut off every trace of Baal, \q the very name of the idol-priests along with the priests,
en.R: I will punish Judah \q and all the people who live in Jerusalem. \q I will remove from this place every last trace of Baal worship. \q Even the names of the priests who serve idols will be forgotten, and the priests who join them.

fr.L: Et j’étendrai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main contre Juda \q et contre tous les habitants de Jérusalem ; \q et je retrancherai de ce lieu le reste de Baal, \q le nom des prêtres des idoles avec les prêtres,
fr.B: J’étendrai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main contre Juda \q et contre tous ceux qui habitent Jérusalem. \q De ce lieu je retrancherai toute trace de Baal, \q jusqu’au nom des prêtres des idoles, avec les prêtres,
fr.R: Je vais punir Juda \q et tous les habitants de Jérusalem. \q Je vais faire disparaître de ce lieu toute trace du culte de Baal. \q On oubliera même le nom des prêtres qui servent les idoles, et celui des prêtres qui se sont joints à eux.

es.L: Y extenderé {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano contra Judá \q y contra todos los habitantes de Jerusalén; \q y exterminaré de este lugar el remanente de Baal, \q el nombre de los sacerdotes idólatras junto con los sacerdotes,
es.B: Extenderé {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano contra Judá \q y contra todos los que viven en Jerusalén. \q De este lugar exterminaré todo rastro de Baal, \q hasta el nombre de los sacerdotes idólatras junto con los sacerdotes,
es.R: Castigaré a Judá \q y a todos los que viven en Jerusalén. \q Quitaré de este lugar hasta el último rastro del culto a Baal. \q Se olvidarán aun los nombres de los sacerdotes que sirven a los ídolos y de los sacerdotes que se les unen.

sw.L: Nami nitaunyosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} dhidi ya Yuda \q na dhidi ya wote wakaao Yerusalemu; \q nami nitakatilia mbali kutoka mahali hapa mabaki ya Baali, \q jina la makuhani wa sanamu pamoja na makuhani,
sw.B: Nitaunyosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} dhidi ya Yuda \q na dhidi ya wote wanaoishi Yerusalemu. \q Kutoka mahali hapa nitaondoa kila alama ya Baali, \q hata jina la makuhani wa sanamu pamoja na makuhani,
sw.R: Nitaiadhibu Yuda \q na watu wote wanaoishi Yerusalemu. \q Nitaondoa mahali hapa kila alama ya mwisho ya ibada ya Baali. \q Hata majina ya makuhani wanaotumikia sanamu yatasahauliwa, pamoja na makuhani wanaojiunga nao.

decisions.choice: stretch out my hand against: act in power to punish
decisions.reason: The outstretched hand of the LORD is his power at work, as when he struck Egypt (Exodus 7:5). In Isaiah his hand is "stretched out still" against his own people (Isaiah 5:25; 9:11). The judgment of the whole world in verses 2-3 now turns on Judah and Jerusalem. |

decisions.choice: the remnant of Baal: whatever is left of the worship of Baal
alternatives: the last survivors of Baal's worshipers
decisions.reason: "Remnant" is what remains of something. Here it means the last trace of Baal worship in Jerusalem, "this place". If the verse comes from the time of Josiah's purge (2 Kings 23:4-5), some of that worship was already gone and the LORD will finish it. |

decisions.choice: the idol-priests with the priests: priests of foreign gods, together with priests who joined them
decisions.reason: The first word is used only of priests who served idols (2 Kings 23:5; Hosea 10:5). The second is the usual word for priests, and here probably means priests of the LORD who took part in the same worship. To cut off someone's name is to wipe out even their memory. |

decisions.choice: idol-priests (L, B); the priests who serve idols (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows Hosea 10:5 and 2 Kings 23:5. Readable says "I will punish" for "stretch out my hand against" (m1) and makes the cutting off of the name plain: the names will be forgotten. |

decisions.choice: "les prêtres des idoles" (L, B) for *kemarim*
decisions.reason: As the published 2 Kings 23:5.

decisions.choice: "sacerdotes idólatras" (L, B); "sacerdotes que sirven a los ídolos" (R)
decisions.reason: The word (kemarim) is used only of priests of other gods; Spanish names them apart from the ordinary "sacerdotes" that follows.

decisions.choice: "makuhani wa sanamu" (L, B); "makuhani wanaotumikia sanamu" (R)
decisions.reason: The kemarim are priests of foreign gods; Swahili names what they are, as the English "idol-priests" does, and keeps them apart from "makuhani", the priests who joined them.

source.text: וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁתַּחֲוִ֥ים עַל־הַגַּגּ֖וֹת לִצְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְאֶת־הַמִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוִים֙ הַנִּשְׁבָּעִ֣ים לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְהַנִּשְׁבָּעִ֖ים בְּמַלְכָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and those who bow down on the roofs to the host of the heavens, and those who bow down, who swear to Yahweh and who swear by their king,

en.L: and those who bow down on the roofs to the host of the heavens, \q and those who bow down, who swear to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and swear by their king,
en.B: those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of heaven, \q and those who bow down and swear by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q while they also swear by their king,
en.R: I will destroy those who bow down on their roofs to worship the stars in the sky. \q I will destroy those who bow down and make promises in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q but also make promises in the name of the god they call their king.

fr.L: et ceux qui se prosternent sur les toits devant l’armée des cieux, \q et ceux qui se prosternent, qui jurent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} \q et jurent par leur roi,
fr.B: ceux qui se prosternent sur les toits devant l’armée des cieux, \q et ceux qui se prosternent et jurent par {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} \q tout en jurant aussi par leur roi,
fr.R: Je vais détruire ceux qui se prosternent sur leurs toits pour adorer les étoiles du ciel. \q Je vais détruire ceux qui se prosternent et font des promesses au nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q mais qui font aussi des promesses au nom du dieu qu’ils appellent leur roi.

es.L: y a los que se postran en las azoteas ante el ejército de los cielos, \q y a los que se postran, que juran {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} \q y juran por su rey,
es.B: a los que se postran en las azoteas ante el ejército del cielo, \q y a los que se postran y juran por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} \q mientras juran también por su rey,
es.R: Destruiré a los que se inclinan en sus azoteas para adorar a las estrellas del cielo. \q Destruiré a los que se inclinan y hacen promesas en el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q pero también hacen promesas en el nombre del dios al que llaman su rey.

sw.L: na wale wanaosujudu juu ya dari kwa jeshi la mbinguni, \q na wale wanaosujudu, wanaoapa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} \q na kuapa kwa mfalme wao,

decisions.choice: worship of the host of heaven on the roofs
decisions.reason: The host of heaven is the sun, moon and stars, worshiped as gods. Flat roofs served as places of worship where the sky could be seen, and people burned incense and poured offerings there (2 Kings 23:12; Jeremiah 19:13; 32:29). Josiah's purge removed this worship (2 Kings 23:5). |

decisions.choice: by their king: by the god they honor as king, perhaps Milcom
decisions.reason: The Hebrew letters can be read "their king" or "Milcom", the god of the Ammonites (1 Kings 11:5, 33; Jeremiah 49:1). The standard Hebrew text reads "their king", and the Greek and Latin traditions are generally said to support Milcom in some copies. Either way the "king" is a god other than the LORD; "king" is also the meaning of the name Molech.

decisions.choice: swear to the LORD and swear by their king: divided loyalty
decisions.reason: To swear by a god is to call on him as witness and to acknowledge his authority. These people bow to the LORD and still keep another god, the half-loyalty Elijah condemned (1 Kings 18:21). Zephaniah lists three groups in verses 4-6: the open idolaters, those who serve the LORD and other gods together, and those who have turned away from the LORD altogether. |

decisions.choice: the host of the heavens (L), the host of heaven (B), the stars in the sky (R); their king at every level
decisions.reason: "The host of heaven" follows Jeremiah 19:13 and 2 Kings 23:5. "Their king" follows the Hebrew text at every level; Readable adds "the god they call" so that the reader knows that a god is meant, which the verse implies (m2). Readable repeats "I will destroy" from verse 4 to make each group its own sentence. |

decisions.choice: "su rey"
decisions.reason: As in the English, "their king" is kept at every level (lowercase) and not turned into the name Milcom; the meaning decision gives that reading.

decisions.choice: seek the LORD, inquire of him: turn to him in worship and prayer, and ask his guidance
decisions.reason: To seek the LORD is to come to him in worship and to live by his will (Amos 5:4-6; Hosea 10:12). To inquire of him is to ask him for guidance, often through a prophet or priest. The last group in verses 4-6 have not taken up other gods; they simply live as if the LORD did not matter. Verse 12 describes their attitude. |

decisions.choice: turn back from following the LORD: give up being his followers
decisions.reason: To walk "after" someone is to follow him as a servant follows his master or worshipers follow a god (Jeremiah 2:5). These people once followed the LORD and have turned their backs. |

decisions.choice: Hush: be silent in awe, because the LORD is about to act
decisions.reason: The word is a call for silence, like "Hush!". People fall silent before a judge or a king who has come to act (Habakkuk 2:20; Zechariah 2:17; Amos 6:10). |

decisions.choice: for near is the day of the LORD: the words of Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15
decisions.reason: "Near is the day of the LORD" is found word for word in Isaiah 13:6, Joel 1:15 and Obadiah 15, and again in verse 14. The day of the LORD is the day when the LORD comes to act in judgment, and to rescue; see the note at Joel 1:15. |

decisions.choice: the LORD's sacrifice: Judah itself is the sacrifice, and the guests are the nations invited to the slaughter
decisions.reason: A sacrifice was often followed by a meal for invited guests, who first made themselves ritually clean (1 Samuel 9:13; 16:5). Here the picture is turned around: the victims are the people of Judah, and the guests are the enemies the LORD summons to carry out his judgment. Isaiah 34:6, Jeremiah 46:10 and Ezekiel 39:17-20 use the same picture of a slaughter as a sacrifice. The poem does not name the guests. |

decisions.choice: consecrated: made holy, made ready to take part
decisions.reason: The verb means "make holy". Guests at a sacrifice were consecrated to take part in it (1 Samuel 16:5). The same verb is used of armies made ready for a holy war (Jeremiah 6:4; Isaiah 13:3, where the LORD calls them "my consecrated ones"). |

decisions.choice: the wording of Isaiah 13:6 at each level; Hush (L), Be silent (B), Be quiet (R)
decisions.reason: Where Zephaniah repeats the words of Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15, each level uses the wording already published there: "near [is] the day of the LORD" (L), "is close at hand" (B), "is near" (R). "The Lord GOD" follows the table for the divine name with "Lord". Balanced and Readable spell out "his invited ones" as the guests he invited or chose. |

decisions.reason: "cerca [está] el día del SEÑOR" (L) and "el día del SEÑOR está cerca" (B, R) reuse the published lines where the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.reason: "The Lord GOD" (Adonai YHWH) is "Bwana MUNGU" at every level, as the term sheet. "The day of the LORD is near" reuses the published Swahili of Isaiah 13:6 at each level. Recorded once for this job.

en.L: And it will be on the day of the sacrifice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q that I will punish the officials and the sons of the king, \q and all who clothe themselves in foreign clothing.
en.B: On the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s sacrifice \q I will punish the officials and the king's sons, \q and all who dress in foreign clothes.
en.R: On the day when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} offers this sacrifice, \q I will punish the leaders and the king's sons \q and everyone who dresses like foreigners.

fr.L: Et il arrivera, au jour du sacrifice {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q que je punirai les chefs et les fils du roi, \q et tous ceux qui s’habillent de vêtements étrangers.
fr.B: Au jour du sacrifice {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q je punirai les chefs et les fils du roi, \q et tous ceux qui portent des vêtements étrangers.
fr.R: Le jour où {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} offrira ce sacrifice, \q je punirai les dirigeants et les fils du roi, \q et tous ceux qui s’habillent comme les étrangers.

decisions.choice: I will punish: I will call to account
decisions.reason: The verb means to visit, inspect or attend to. With "on" a person it means to call him to account and punish him, as again in verses 9 and 12. |

decisions.choice: the officials and the sons of the king: the leaders of the court and the royal family
decisions.reason: The king himself is not named. Josiah came to the throne at eight years old (2 Kings 22:1), and the officials who ran the kingdom, with the royal princes, were the ones who shaped its life. Judgment begins with those who lead. |

decisions.choice: foreign clothing: dress taken from other nations, perhaps for their worship
decisions.reason: Clothes showed which people, and which god, one belonged to. Worshipers of Baal wore special robes (2 Kings 10:22). Foreign dress may mean the garments of foreign worship, or a wider taking over of foreign ways by Judah's leaders. Either way it marks loyalty given away from the LORD.

decisions.choice: officials (L, B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the one settled for court officials in the Twelve. Readable says "everyone who dresses like foreigners" for "clothe themselves in foreign clothing". |

decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for *sarim* in the Twelve.

decisions.choice: "príncipes" (L), "jefes" (B), "dirigentes" (R)
decisions.reason: Human sarim follow the Spanish prophets' words at each level, against the English Twelve's "officials", as the term sheet sets (uncertain).

decisions.reason: Sar is "officials" at L and B and "leaders" at R in the English of the Twelve; Swahili follows with "maafisa" and "viongozi".

sw.B: Siku hiyo nitawaadhibu wote wanaoruka juu ya kizingiti, \q na wanaoijaza nyumba ya bwana wao dhuluma na udanganyifu.

decisions.choice: who leaps over the threshold: a practice of foreign worship, or a forced entry
alternatives: those who climb onto the platform
those who burst into houses to rob them
decisions.reason: When the idol of Dagon fell on its threshold, his priests began to avoid stepping on it (1 Samuel 5:5). Leaping over the threshold may be a custom like that, taken over from foreign worship, which fits verse 8. The word may also mean a raised platform, or the verse may picture servants rushing through doors to seize goods for their master, which fits the second half of the verse. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: their master: their lord, the king or the god they serve
decisions.reason: The word is plural in form, which Hebrew uses for one master and for God. It may be the king, whose palace his servants fill with plunder, or a god, whose temple is filled. The first fits the verse best.

decisions.choice: fill with violence and deceit: fill with goods gained by violence and fraud
decisions.reason: Amos 3:10 speaks of those who "store up violence and robbery in their fortresses", and Jeremiah 5:27 of houses "full of deceit". What is meant is the plunder itself, named by the way it was gained. |

decisions.choice: with what they have taken by violence and lies (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what fills the house (m3). |

decisions.choice: in that day (L), on that day (B), at that time (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the Isaiah table, here and in verse 10. |

decisions.reason: "In that day" as the Isaiah block sets it; recorded once for this job.

fr.L: Et il arrivera en ce jour-là, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le bruit d’un cri depuis la porte des Poissons, \q et une lamentation depuis le second [quartier], \q et un grand fracas depuis les collines.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, un cri s’élèvera de la porte des Poissons, \q une lamentation du second quartier, \q et un grand fracas des collines.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, les gens crieront à la porte des Poissons. \q Ils se lamenteront dans le second quartier, la partie nouvelle de la ville. \q Un grand bruit d’effondrement viendra des collines.

es.L: Y sucederá en aquel día, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, [que habrá] voz de clamor desde la puerta del Pescado, \q y gemido desde el Segundo Barrio, \q y gran estruendo desde las colinas.
es.B: Aquel día, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, se oirá un clamor desde la puerta del Pescado, \q gemidos desde el Segundo Barrio \q y un gran estruendo desde las colinas.
es.R: En ese tiempo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, la gente gritará en la puerta del Pescado. \q Llorarán en el Segundo Barrio, la parte nueva de la ciudad. \q Se oirá un gran estruendo desde las colinas.

sw.L: Na itakuwa katika siku ile, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, sauti ya kilio kutoka Lango la Samaki, \q na maombolezo kutoka Mtaa wa Pili, \q na kishindo kikuu kutoka vilimani.
sw.B: Siku hiyo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kilio kitapanda kutoka Lango la Samaki, \q maombolezo kutoka Mtaa wa Pili, \q na kishindo kikubwa kutoka vilimani.
sw.R: Wakati huo, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, watu watalia kwenye Lango la Samaki. \q Wataomboleza katika Mtaa wa Pili, sehemu mpya ya mji. \q Sauti kubwa ya kitu kinachovunjika itasikika kutoka vilimani.

decisions.choice: the Fish Gate and the Second Quarter: parts of Jerusalem on its northern side
decisions.reason: The Fish Gate was in the northern wall of Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 33:14; Nehemiah 3:3), perhaps named for the fish brought there to market. The Second Quarter was a newer district of the city, where the prophetess Huldah lived (2 Kings 22:14). An enemy attacking Jerusalem usually came from the north, where the ground is level, so the cries begin there. The hills are those on which the city stood. |

decisions.choice: a great crash: the noise of something breaking and falling
decisions.reason: The word means a breaking or shattering. It is the sound of walls and houses falling as the city is taken, heard from the hills of Jerusalem. |

decisions.choice: the Second Quarter, the newer part of the city (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the Second Quarter was (m1) and makes each cry its own sentence. |

decisions.choice: "la porte des Poissons"; "le second [quartier]" (L), "le second quartier" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the published 2 Chronicles 33:14 and 2 Kings 22:14, where the same places are named.

decisions.choice: "la puerta del Pescado"; "el Segundo Barrio"
decisions.reason: The Fish Gate keeps the Spanish of 2 Chronicles 33:14 and Nehemiah; the city's second district is "el Segundo Barrio", as 2 Kings 22:14 in Spanish.

decisions.choice: "Lango la Samaki", "Mtaa wa Pili"
decisions.reason: The names of the gate and the district as the published Nehemiah 3:3 and 2 Kings 22:14 give them.

source.text: הֵילִ֖ילוּ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הַמַּכְתֵּ֑שׁ כִּ֤י נִדְמָה֙ כָּל־עַ֣ם כְּנַ֔עַן נִכְרְת֖וּ כָּל־נְטִ֥ילֵי כָֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: Wail, inhabitants of the Mortar, for all [the] people of Canaan are destroyed; cut off [are] all who weigh out silver.

en.L: Wail, inhabitants of the Mortar, \q for all the people of Canaan are destroyed; \q cut off are all who weigh out silver.
en.B: Wail, you who live in the Mortar, \q for all the merchants are destroyed; \q all who trade with silver are cut off.
en.R: Cry out in grief, you who live in the part of the city called the Mortar! \q All the traders will be destroyed. \q Everyone who buys and sells for silver will be wiped out.

fr.L: Lamentez-vous, habitants du Mortier, \q car tout le peuple de Canaan est détruit ; \q retranchés sont tous ceux qui pèsent l’argent.
fr.B: Lamentez-vous, vous qui habitez le Mortier, \q car tous les marchands sont anéantis ; \q tous ceux qui manient l’argent sont retranchés.
fr.R: Criez de douleur, vous qui habitez le quartier qu’on appelle le Mortier ! \q Tous les commerçants seront détruits. \q Tous ceux qui achètent et vendent avec de l’argent disparaîtront.

es.L: {{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, habitantes del Mortero, \q porque todo el pueblo de Canaán ha sido destruido; \q exterminados [son] todos los que pesan plata.
es.B: {{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que viven en el Mortero, \q porque todos los comerciantes han sido destruidos; \q todos los que negocian con plata han sido exterminados.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Lloren|Llorad}} de dolor, {{plural_you:ustedes que viven|vosotros que vivís}} en la parte de la ciudad llamada el Mortero! \q Todos los comerciantes serán destruidos. \q Todos los que compran y venden con plata serán eliminados.

sw.L: Ombolezeni, enyi wakaaji wa Kinu, \q kwa maana watu wote wa Kanaani wameangamizwa; \q wamekatiliwa mbali wote wanaopima fedha.
sw.B: Ombolezeni, ninyi mnaoishi katika Kinu, \q kwa maana wafanyabiashara wote wameangamizwa; \q wote wanaofanya biashara kwa fedha wamekatiliwa mbali.
sw.R: Lieni kwa huzuni, ninyi mnaoishi katika sehemu ya mji inayoitwa Kinu! \q Wafanyabiashara wote wataangamizwa. \q Kila anayenunua na kuuza kwa fedha atafutiliwa mbali.

decisions.choice: the Mortar: a district of Jerusalem, probably a hollow where the market was
decisions.reason: The word means a mortar, a bowl for pounding grain, and is used of a hollow in the ground (Judges 15:19). Here it is a part of Jerusalem, probably in the valley that runs through the city, where traders did business. The name also suggests that its people will be pounded as in a mortar.

decisions.choice: the people of Canaan: the traders
decisions.reason: The Canaanites, and especially the Phoenicians of the coast, were known as traders, so "Canaanite" came to mean "merchant" (Hosea 12:8; Proverbs 31:24; Isaiah 23:8). The parallel line, "all who weigh out silver", shows that this is the sense here. |

decisions.choice: who weigh out silver: those who handle money in trade
decisions.reason: There were no coins yet in Judah. Payment was made by weighing out silver on scales (Genesis 23:16; Jeremiah 32:9). |

decisions.choice: Wail (L, B), Cry out in grief (R); the people of Canaan (L), the merchants (B), the traders (R)
decisions.reason: "Wail" follows the Isaiah table for this cry. Literal keeps "the people of Canaan" and Balanced and Readable give its sense (m2). |

decisions.choice: "Giman" (L, B); "Lloren de dolor" (R), with plural_you
decisions.reason: The call to wail follows the Spanish of Isaiah 13:6 at each level.

decisions.choice: "el Mortero"
decisions.reason: The district's name means a mortar or hollow; Spanish translates it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Kinu" (the Mortar)
decisions.reason: The district is named by translating it, as the English does: "kinu" is the mortar for pounding grain, which pictures the hollow where the market stood.

source.text: וְהָיָה֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא אֲחַפֵּ֥שׂ אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּנֵּר֑וֹת וּפָקַדְתִּ֣י עַל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַקֹּֽפְאִים֙ עַל־שִׁמְרֵיהֶ֔ם הָאֹֽמְרִים֙ בִּלְבָבָ֔ם לֹֽא־יֵיטִ֥יב יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יָרֵֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be at that time, I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish the men who are thickening on their dregs, who say in their heart, Yahweh will not do good and will not do harm.

en.L: And it will be at that time \q that I will search through Jerusalem with lamps, \q and I will punish the {{gender:people|men}} who are thickening on their dregs, \q who say in their heart, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not do good, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not do harm."
en.B: At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps \q and punish those who are complacent, \q like wine left to thicken on its dregs, \q who say to themselves, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will do nothing, neither good nor bad."
en.R: At that time I will search every corner of Jerusalem with lamps. \q I will punish the people who are lazy and satisfied with themselves, like wine left too long on its dregs. \q They think, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not do anything, good or bad."

fr.L: Et il arrivera en ce temps-là \q que je fouillerai Jérusalem avec des lampes, \q et je punirai les {{gender:gens|hommes}} qui s’épaississent sur leur lie, \q qui disent dans leur cœur : \q « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne fera pas de bien, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne fera pas de mal. »
fr.B: En ce temps-là, je fouillerai Jérusalem avec des lampes \q et je punirai ceux qui se reposent, tranquilles, \q comme le vin laissé à s’épaissir sur sa lie, \q ceux qui se disent : \q « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne fera rien, ni bien ni mal. »
fr.R: En ce temps-là, je fouillerai chaque recoin de Jérusalem avec des lampes. \q Je punirai les gens paresseux et contents d’eux-mêmes, comme du vin resté trop longtemps sur sa lie. \q Ils pensent : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne fera rien, ni en bien ni en mal. »

es.L: Y sucederá en aquel tiempo \q que escudriñaré Jerusalén con lámparas, \q y castigaré a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que se espesan sobre sus heces, \q que dicen en su corazón: \q «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no hará bien, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no hará mal».
es.B: En aquel tiempo registraré Jerusalén con lámparas \q y castigaré a los que están satisfechos de sí mismos, \q como el vino que se deja espesar sobre sus heces, \q y que piensan: \q «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no hará nada, ni bueno ni malo».
es.R: En ese tiempo buscaré con lámparas por todos los rincones de Jerusalén. \q Castigaré a la gente perezosa y satisfecha de sí misma, como el vino que se deja demasiado tiempo sobre sus heces. \q Ellos piensan: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no hará nada, ni bueno ni malo».

sw.L: Na itakuwa wakati ule \q kwamba nitaipekua Yerusalemu kwa taa, \q nami nitawaadhibu watu wanaoganda juu ya mashapo yao, \q wanaosema mioyoni mwao, \q "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatatenda mema, wala hatatenda mabaya."
sw.B: Wakati huo nitaipekua Yerusalemu kwa taa \q na kuwaadhibu wale walioridhika na kutulia, \q kama divai iliyoachwa iganda juu ya mashapo yake, \q wanaosema mioyoni mwao, \q "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatafanya lolote, jema wala baya."
sw.R: Wakati huo nitaipekua kila kona ya Yerusalemu kwa taa. \q Nitawaadhibu watu walio wavivu na wanaojiridhisha, kama divai iliyoachwa muda mrefu juu ya mashapo yake. \q Wanafikiri, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatafanya chochote, kizuri wala kibaya."

decisions.choice: search Jerusalem with lamps: search every dark corner, so that no one escapes
decisions.reason: A lamp was needed to search a house thoroughly (Luke 15:8). The picture is of a search from which no one can hide (Amos 9:2-3). |

decisions.choice: thickening on their dregs: settled, complacent, unmoved
decisions.reason: Wine was left on its dregs for a time to gain strength and flavor, but if it was left too long it thickened and turned syrupy. Jeremiah 48:11 says that Moab has "settled on its dregs" because it was never poured from vessel to vessel. The people are comfortable and stagnant, untouched by any change. |

decisions.choice: will not do good and will not do harm: will do nothing at all
decisions.reason: Naming two opposites means "anything at all" (Jeremiah 10:5; Isaiah 41:23). They do not deny that the LORD exists; they think he will not act, so they need not take him into account. The day of the LORD answers them. |

decisions.choice: the people (L, gender default), those who (B)
decisions.reason: The word means men, but here it stands for the complacent people of Jerusalem, women and men alike, so Literal uses the gender setting and Balanced says "those who". |

decisions.choice: complacent, like wine left to thicken on its dregs (B); lazy and satisfied with themselves (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m2) and keep the picture itself. The people's words are set in double quotes as speech quoted inside the oracle. |

decisions.choice: {{gender:gens|hommes}} (L), as the English {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "men" here means the complacent people of Jerusalem in general, so French Literal carries the same setting as the English: "gens" by default, "hommes" as the traditional wording.

decisions.choice: {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "men", but the whole city is meant; L follows the English with a gender span. B and R say "los que" and "la gente", which already include women.

decisions.choice: "watu" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span on "people / men"; Swahili "watu" already covers men and women, and "wanaume" would change the meaning, so there is no span. Recorded once for this job.

source.text: וְהָיָ֤ה חֵילָם֙ לִמְשִׁסָּ֔ה וּבָתֵּיהֶ֖ם לִשְׁמָמָ֑ה וּבָנ֤וּ בָתִּים֙ וְלֹ֣א יֵשֵׁ֔בוּ וְנָטְע֣וּ כְרָמִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁתּ֖וּ אֶת־יֵינָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And their wealth will become plunder, and their houses a desolation; and they will build houses and not dwell [in them], and they will plant vineyards and not drink their wine.

en.L: And their wealth will become plunder, \q and their houses a desolation; \q they will build houses but not dwell [in them], \q and they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.
en.B: Their wealth will be plundered \q and their houses left in ruins. \q They will build houses but not live in them; \q they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.
en.R: Their riches will be stolen, \q and their houses will be destroyed. \q They will build houses, but they will never live in them. \q They will plant vineyards, but they will never drink the wine.

fr.L: Et leurs richesses deviendront un butin, \q et leurs maisons une désolation ; \q ils bâtiront des maisons mais n’[y] habiteront pas, \q et ils planteront des vignes mais n’en boiront pas le vin.
fr.B: Leurs richesses seront pillées \q et leurs maisons laissées en ruines. \q Ils bâtiront des maisons mais n’y habiteront pas ; \q ils planteront des vignes mais n’en boiront pas le vin.
fr.R: On volera leurs richesses, \q et leurs maisons seront détruites. \q Ils construiront des maisons, mais ils n’y habiteront jamais. \q Ils planteront des vignes, mais ils n’en boiront jamais le vin.

es.L: Y sus riquezas serán botín, \q y sus casas, desolación; \q edificarán casas, pero no [las] habitarán, \q y plantarán viñas, pero no beberán su vino.
es.B: Sus riquezas serán saqueadas \q y sus casas quedarán en ruinas. \q Construirán casas, pero no vivirán en ellas; \q plantarán viñas, pero no beberán su vino.
es.R: Les robarán sus riquezas, \q y sus casas serán destruidas. \q Construirán casas, pero nunca vivirán en ellas. \q Plantarán viñas, pero nunca beberán el vino.

sw.L: Na mali zao zitakuwa nyara, \q na nyumba zao ukiwa; \q watajenga nyumba lakini hawatakaa [ndani yake], \q na watapanda mashamba ya mizabibu lakini hawatakunywa divai yake.
sw.B: Mali zao zitatekwa nyara \q na nyumba zao zitaachwa magofu. \q Watajenga nyumba lakini hawataishi ndani yake; \q watapanda mashamba ya mizabibu lakini hawatakunywa divai yake.
sw.R: Utajiri wao utaibiwa, \q na nyumba zao zitaharibiwa. \q Watajenga nyumba, lakini hawataishi ndani yake kamwe. \q Watapanda mashamba ya mizabibu, lakini hawatakunywa divai yake kamwe.

decisions.choice: build houses and not dwell in them, plant vineyards and not drink their wine: the curse of the covenant
decisions.reason: These are among the curses of Deuteronomy 28:30, 39 on a people who break the covenant, and Amos 5:11 uses them against Israel. The complacent who said that the LORD would do nothing (verse 12) find that he does what he warned he would do. Isaiah 65:21-22 turns the curse into a promise. |

decisions.choice: [in them] (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "and not dwell"; Literal brackets the words English needs. |

source.text: קָר֤וֹב יוֹם־יְהוָה֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל קָר֖וֹב וּמַהֵ֣ר מְאֹ֑ד ק֚וֹל י֣וֹם יְהוָ֔ה מַ֥ר צֹרֵ֖חַ שָׁ֥ם גִּבּֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Near [is] the great day of Yahweh, near and hastening greatly; [the] sound of [the] day of Yahweh; bitterly a warrior cries out there.

en.L: Near [is] the great day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q near and hastening fast; \q the sound of the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Bitterly the warrior cries out there.
en.B: The great day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is close at hand, \q close and coming very fast. \q Listen! The day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q There the warrior cries out in bitter anguish.
en.R: The great day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is near. \q It is coming closer, and coming fast. \q Listen! It is the sound of the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Even strong soldiers will cry out bitterly then.

fr.L: Il est proche, le grand jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q proche et se hâtant très vite ; \q le bruit du jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! \q Amèrement le guerrier crie là.
fr.B: Le grand jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est tout proche, \q il est proche et arrive très vite. \q Écoutez ! Le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! \q Là, le guerrier pousse un cri d’angoisse amère.
fr.R: Le grand jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est proche. \q Il se rapproche, et il arrive vite. \q Écoutez ! C’est le bruit du jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Ce jour-là, même les soldats les plus forts pousseront des cris amers.

es.L: Cerca [está] el gran día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q cerca y se apresura mucho; \q ¡el sonido del día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q Amargamente grita allí el guerrero.
es.B: El gran día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está cerca, \q cerca y viene muy deprisa. \q ¡Escucha! ¡El día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q Allí el guerrero grita con amarga angustia.
es.R: El gran día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está cerca. \q Se acerca, y viene rápido. \q ¡Escucha! Es el ruido del día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q Entonces hasta los soldados fuertes gritarán con amargura.

sw.L: Siku kuu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [i] karibu, \q [i] karibu na inaharakisha sana; \q sauti ya siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Shujaa analia kwa uchungu huko.
sw.B: Siku kuu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} imekaribia, \q iko karibu na inakuja kwa kasi sana. \q Sikiliza! Siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Huko shujaa analia kwa uchungu mkuu.
sw.R: Siku kuu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} iko karibu. \q Inakaribia, tena inakuja kwa kasi. \q Sikilizeni! Ni sauti ya siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Hata askari hodari watalia kwa uchungu wakati huo.

decisions.choice: the great day of the LORD: the day when the LORD comes to judge
decisions.reason: Verses 14-18 are the fullest description in the prophets of the day of the LORD, the day when the LORD comes to act against all that is proud and wicked. See the note at Joel 1:15. Zephaniah takes up the words of Isaiah 13:6 ("near is the day of the LORD") and Joel 2:2 ("a day of darkness and gloom", verse 15). |

decisions.choice: the sound of the day of the LORD! Bitterly the warrior cries out
alternatives: the sound of the day of the LORD is bitter; the warrior cries out there
decisions.reason: The Hebrew accents divide the line after "the day of the LORD", so that "bitter" goes with the warrior's cry. Without the accents the words could be read "the sound of the day of the LORD is bitter". The sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: the warrior cries out there: even the strongest soldier cries out in distress
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a mighty warrior. On that day even he will cry out in distress, not in triumph (Amos 2:14-16; Jeremiah 46:5-6). "There" points to the scene of the day. |

decisions.choice: the wording of Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15 at each level
decisions.reason: "Near [is] the day of the LORD" (L), "is close at hand" (B) and "is near" (R) are the wording published in Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15, as set for the day of the LORD in the Twelve. Balanced and Readable say "Listen!" for "the sound of", as an exclamation. Readable says "then" for "there", because the line speaks of what will happen on the day. |

decisions.choice: the Spanish wording of Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15
decisions.reason: "Cerca [está] el ... día del SEÑOR" (L) and "el ... día del SEÑOR está cerca" (B, R) are kept as in verse 7 and the published parallels.

decisions.choice: "¡Escucha!"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "sound" works as a call to listen; Spanish uses the singular, addressed to any hearer, so there is no plural_you span.

source.text: י֥וֹם עֶבְרָ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא י֧וֹם צָרָ֣ה וּמְצוּקָ֗ה י֤וֹם שֹׁאָה֙ וּמְשׁוֹאָ֔ה י֥וֹם חֹ֨שֶׁךְ֙ וַאֲפֵלָ֔ה י֥וֹם עָנָ֖ן וַעֲרָפֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: A day of fury [is] that day, a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness,

en.L: A day of fury [is] that day, \q a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation, \q a day of darkness and gloom, \q a day of clouds and thick darkness,
en.B: That day will be a day of fury, \q a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation, \q a day of darkness and gloom, \q a day of clouds and deep darkness,
en.R: That day will be a day of terrible anger, \q a day of trouble and pain, a day of ruin and destruction, \q a dark and gloomy day, a day of black clouds,

fr.L: Un jour de fureur, ce jour-là, \q un jour de détresse et d’angoisse, un jour de ruine et de dévastation, \q un jour de ténèbres et d’obscurité, \q un jour de nuées et de brume épaisse,
fr.B: Ce jour sera un jour de fureur, \q un jour de détresse et d’angoisse, un jour de ruine et de dévastation, \q un jour de ténèbres et d’obscurité, \q un jour de nuages et de nuit épaisse,
fr.R: Ce jour sera un jour de terrible colère, \q un jour de malheur et de souffrance, un jour de ruine et de destruction, \q un jour sombre et triste, un jour de nuages noirs,

es.L: Día de furor [es] aquel día, \q día de angustia y aflicción, día de ruina y devastación, \q día de tinieblas y oscuridad, \q día de nubes y densas tinieblas,
es.B: Aquel día será un día de furor, \q un día de angustia y aflicción, un día de ruina y devastación, \q un día de tinieblas y oscuridad, \q un día de nubes y negrura,
es.R: Aquel día será un día de terrible enojo, \q un día de problemas y dolor, un día de ruina y destrucción, \q un día oscuro y sombrío, un día de nubes negras,

sw.L: Siku ya ghadhabu [ni] siku ile, \q siku ya dhiki na taabu, siku ya uharibifu na ukiwa, \q siku ya giza na utusitusi, \q siku ya mawingu na giza nene,
sw.B: Siku ile itakuwa siku ya ghadhabu, \q siku ya dhiki na taabu, siku ya uharibifu na ukiwa, \q siku ya giza na utusitusi, \q siku ya mawingu na giza nene,
sw.R: Siku ile itakuwa siku ya hasira kali, \q siku ya shida na maumivu, siku ya uharibifu na maangamizi, \q siku ya giza na huzuni, siku ya mawingu meusi,

decisions.choice: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness: the words of Joel 2:2
decisions.reason: The same four words describe the day of the LORD in Joel 2:2. Clouds and thick darkness also surrounded the LORD when he came down on Mount Sinai (Deuteronomy 4:11; Exodus 20:21): the day is the coming of God himself. Amos had said that the day would be darkness, not light (Amos 5:18-20). |

decisions.choice: distress and anguish, ruin and devastation: pairs of words that sound alike
decisions.reason: Each pair joins two words of the same sound and sense, for emphasis. The second pair is especially close in sound (sho'ah umesho'ah). The six pairs hammer home the one day. |

decisions.choice: a day of fury is that day: the words behind the hymn "Dies irae"
decisions.reason: In the Latin translation this line begins "dies irae, dies illa" ("a day of wrath, that day"). The medieval Latin hymn on the last judgment that begins with these words, the "Dies irae", was long sung in the Western church's mass for the dead. |

decisions.choice: the wording of Joel 2:2 at each level
decisions.reason: Where Zephaniah repeats Joel 2:2, each level uses the wording published there: "a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness" (L), "a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and deep darkness" (B), "a dark and gloomy day, a day of black clouds" (R). "Fury" follows Isaiah 13:9 at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "terrible anger", as there. |

decisions.choice: The published Joel 2:2 words at each level ("un jour de ténèbres et d'obscurité, un jour de nuées et de brume épaisse" L; "… de nuages et de nuit épaisse" B; "un jour sombre et triste, un jour de nuages noirs" R)
decisions.reason: Zephaniah uses the same four nouns as Joel 2:2, so French reuses the published Joel at each level.

decisions.choice: the Spanish wording of Joel 2:2
decisions.reason: The last two lines reuse the published Spanish of Joel 2:2 at each level.

decisions.choice: "siku ya giza na utusitusi, siku ya mawingu na giza nene" (L, B); "siku ya giza na huzuni, siku ya mawingu meusi" (R)
decisions.reason: These are the words of Joel 2:2, so each level reuses the published Swahili of that verse. "Ghadhabu" is kept for the fury (L, B); Readable has "hasira kali".

source.text: י֥וֹם שׁוֹפָ֖ר וּתְרוּעָ֑ה עַ֚ל הֶעָרִ֣ים הַבְּצֻר֔וֹת וְעַ֖ל הַפִּנּ֥וֹת הַגְּבֹהֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: a day of trumpet and battle cry against the fortified cities and against the high corners.

en.L: a day of trumpet and battle cry \q against the fortified cities \q and against the high corners.
en.B: a day of the ram's horn and the battle cry \q against the fortified cities \q and against the lofty corner towers.
en.R: a day when trumpets sound and soldiers shout for battle \q against the strong cities with walls \q and against the high towers at their corners.

fr.L: un jour de cor et de cri de guerre \q contre les villes fortifiées \q et contre les angles élevés.
fr.B: un jour de cor et de cri de guerre \q contre les villes fortifiées \q et contre les hautes tours d’angle.
fr.R: un jour où les trompettes sonnent et où les soldats poussent le cri de guerre \q contre les villes fortes entourées de murailles \q et contre les hautes tours à leurs angles.

es.L: día de trompeta y grito de guerra \q contra las ciudades fortificadas \q y contra las altas esquinas.
es.B: día del cuerno de carnero y del grito de guerra \q contra las ciudades fortificadas \q y contra las altas torres de las esquinas.
es.R: un día en que sonarán las trompetas y los soldados gritarán para la batalla \q contra las ciudades fuertes con murallas \q y contra las altas torres de sus esquinas.

sw.L: siku ya baragumu na kelele za vita \q dhidi ya miji yenye ngome \q na dhidi ya pembe zilizo juu.
sw.B: siku ya baragumu na kelele za vita \q dhidi ya miji yenye ngome \q na dhidi ya minara mirefu ya pembeni.
sw.R: siku ambayo baragumu zitapigwa na askari watapiga kelele za vita \q dhidi ya miji yenye nguvu na kuta \q na dhidi ya minara mirefu iliyo pembeni mwa kuta zake.

decisions.choice: trumpet and battle cry: the signals of an attack
decisions.reason: The ram's horn was blown to sound the alarm or the attack, and the army raised a shout as it charged (Amos 2:2; Jeremiah 4:19). |

decisions.choice: the high corner towers: the towers or battlements at the corners of city walls
decisions.reason: The word means "corners", and on walls it means the corner towers, the strongest points of the defenses (2 Chronicles 26:15). Even they will not stand. |

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R), ram's horn (B); high corners (L), corner towers (B), towers at their corners (R)
decisions.reason: The ram's horn (shofar) follows the Isaiah table. Literal keeps the word "corners"; Balanced and Readable say what the corners of a wall are (m2). |

decisions.choice: *shofar* "cor" (L, B), "trompettes" (R)
decisions.reason: The French prophets' settled wording for the shofar (Isaiah, Jeremiah, Joel): "cor" names the animal horn.

decisions.choice: "trompeta" (L, R); "cuerno de carnero" (B)
decisions.reason: Shofar follows the Spanish of Isaiah at each level.

decisions.choice: "baragumu" at every level
decisions.reason: The shofar is "baragumu" at every level, as in Isaiah, Jeremiah and Joel 2:1; the English varies trumpet and ram's horn, but "baragumu" is already the Swahili word for the horn.

source.text: וַהֲצֵרֹ֣תִי לָאָדָ֗ם וְהָֽלְכוּ֙ כַּֽעִוְרִ֔ים כִּ֥י לַֽיהוָ֖ה חָטָ֑אוּ וְשֻׁפַּ֤ךְ דָּמָם֙ כֶּֽעָפָ֔ר וּלְחֻמָ֖ם כַּגְּלָלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will bring distress on humankind, and they will walk like the blind, for against Yahweh they have sinned; and their blood will be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung.

en.L: And I will bring distress on humankind, and they will walk like the blind, \q for against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they have sinned; \q and their blood will be poured out as dust, \q and their flesh as dung.
en.B: I will bring such distress on people that they will grope like the blind, \q for they have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Their blood will be spilled out like dust \q and their flesh like dung.
en.R: I will bring trouble on people. They will stumble around like blind people, \q because they have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Their blood will be spilled like dust, \q and their dead bodies will lie on the ground like dung.

fr.L: Et j’amènerai la détresse sur l’humanité, et ils marcheront comme les aveugles, \q car contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ils ont péché ; \q et leur sang sera répandu comme de la poussière, \q et leur chair comme du fumier.
fr.B: J’accablerai les humains d’une telle détresse qu’ils marcheront à tâtons comme des aveugles, \q car ils ont péché contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Leur sang sera répandu comme de la poussière \q et leur chair comme du fumier.
fr.R: J’enverrai le malheur sur les gens. Ils trébucheront comme des aveugles, \q parce qu’ils ont péché contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Leur sang sera versé comme de la poussière, \q et leurs cadavres resteront sur le sol comme du fumier.

es.L: Y traeré angustia sobre la humanidad, y andarán como ciegos, \q porque contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} han pecado; \q y su sangre será derramada como polvo, \q y su carne como estiércol.
es.B: Traeré tanta angustia sobre la gente que andarán a tientas como ciegos, \q porque han pecado contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q Su sangre será derramada como polvo, \q y su carne como estiércol.
es.R: Traeré problemas sobre la gente. Andarán tropezando como ciegos, \q porque han pecado contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q Su sangre será derramada como polvo, \q y sus cadáveres quedarán tirados en el suelo como estiércol.

sw.L: Nami nitaleta dhiki juu ya wanadamu, nao watatembea kama vipofu, \q kwa maana wamemtenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} dhambi; \q na damu yao itamwagwa kama vumbi, \q na nyama yao kama mavi.
sw.B: Nitawaletea watu dhiki kiasi kwamba watapapasa kama vipofu, \q kwa maana wamemtenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} dhambi. \q Damu yao itamwagwa kama vumbi \q na nyama yao kama mavi.
sw.R: Nitawaletea watu taabu. Watajikwaa huku na huko kama vipofu, \q kwa sababu wamemtenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} dhambi. \q Damu yao itamwagwa kama vumbi, \q na maiti zao zitalala chini kama mavi.

decisions.choice: they will walk like the blind: the covenant curse of Deuteronomy 28:28-29
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy warns that a disobedient people will grope at noon as a blind man gropes in the dark. Those who did not seek the LORD (verse 6) will not find their way. |

decisions.choice: their flesh: their bodies, perhaps their bowels
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It is used in Job 20:23 for the body, and a related Arabic word means flesh. Some take it as the inner parts of the body. Either way, the bodies of the dead are thrown out like dung.

decisions.choice: poured out like dust: poured out in great quantity and treated as worthless
decisions.reason: Dust is everywhere and has no value. Blood, which stood for life and was to be covered (Leviticus 17:13), is spilled like dirt on the ground. |

decisions.choice: their dead bodies will lie on the ground like dung (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says that the bodies are of the dead, and that they lie unburied, which the picture means. |

source.text: גַּם־כַּסְפָּ֨ם גַּם־זְהָבָ֜ם לֹֽא־יוּכַ֣ל לְהַצִּילָ֗ם בְּיוֹם֙ עֶבְרַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וּבְאֵשׁ֙ קִנְאָת֔וֹ תֵּאָכֵ֖ל כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־כָלָ֤ה אַךְ־נִבְהָלָה֙ יַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה אֵ֥ת כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֖י הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Also their silver, also their gold will not be able to deliver them on [the] day of [the] fury of Yahweh; and in [the] fire of his jealousy all the earth will be consumed; for an end, yes, a terrifying [one], he will make of all [the] inhabitants of the earth.

en.L: Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to rescue them \q on the day of the fury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q and in the fire of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} jealousy all the earth will be consumed; \q for a full end, indeed a terrifying one, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make \q of all the inhabitants of the earth.
en.B: Neither their silver nor their gold \q will be able to save them on the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s fury. \q In the fire of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} jealous anger the whole earth will be consumed, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make an end, a sudden and terrible end, \q of all who live on the earth.
en.R: Their silver and gold will not be able to save them \q on the day when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shows {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger. \q His jealous anger will burn like fire and destroy the whole earth. \q He will suddenly put an end to everyone who lives on the earth.

fr.L: Ni leur argent ni leur or ne pourront les délivrer \q au jour de la fureur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; \q et dans le feu de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} jalousie toute la terre sera dévorée ; \q car c’est une destruction totale, oui, terrifiante, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fera \q de tous les habitants de la terre.
fr.B: Ni leur argent ni leur or \q ne pourront les sauver au jour de la fureur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Dans le feu de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère jalouse, toute la terre sera dévorée, \q car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} mettra fin, une fin soudaine et terrible, \q à tous ceux qui habitent la terre.
fr.R: Leur argent et leur or ne pourront pas les sauver \q le jour où {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} montrera {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère. \q Sa colère jalouse brûlera comme un feu et détruira toute la terre. \q Il mettra fin d’un coup à tous ceux qui vivent sur la terre.

es.L: Ni su plata ni su oro podrán librarlos \q en el día del furor {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; \q y en el fuego de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} celo será consumida toda la tierra; \q porque un final completo, sí, terrible, hará {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} \q de todos los habitantes de la tierra.
es.B: Ni su plata ni su oro \q podrán salvarlos en el día del furor {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q En el fuego de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} celo será consumida toda la tierra, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pondrá fin, un fin repentino y terrible, \q a todos los que viven en la tierra.
es.R: Su plata y su oro no podrán salvarlos \q en el día en que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} muestre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enojo. \q Su celo ardiente quemará como fuego y destruirá toda la tierra. \q De repente acabará con todos los que viven en la tierra.

sw.L: Fedha yao wala dhahabu yao haitaweza kuwaokoa \q katika siku ya ghadhabu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q na katika moto wa wivu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} dunia yote itateketezwa; \q kwa maana ataleta mwisho kamili, naam, mwisho wa kutisha, \q kwa wote wakaao duniani.
sw.B: Fedha yao wala dhahabu yao \q haitaweza kuwaokoa katika siku ya ghadhabu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Katika moto wa wivu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} dunia yote itateketezwa, \q kwa maana atawaletea mwisho, mwisho wa ghafla na wa kutisha, \q wote wanaoishi duniani.
sw.R: Fedha na dhahabu yao haitaweza kuwaokoa \q siku ile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakapoonyesha hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Wivu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} utawaka kama moto na kuiangamiza dunia yote. \q Ghafla atawakomesha wote wanaoishi duniani.

decisions.choice: their silver and their gold will not be able to deliver them: the words of Ezekiel 7:19
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 7:19 says almost the same of the day of the LORD's wrath. The wealth the merchants of verse 11 gathered cannot buy them off. |

decisions.choice: his jealousy: his burning zeal for what is his, not envy
decisions.reason: The LORD's jealousy is the passion with which he claims the loyalty owed to him alone, as a husband claims his wife's (Exodus 20:5; Deuteronomy 4:24, "a consuming fire, a jealous God"). The same line returns in 3:8. |

decisions.choice: terrifying: sudden and dreadful
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning both "terrify" and "hurry". The end will come quickly, and it will be terrible.

decisions.choice: all the earth ... all the inhabitants of the earth: the whole world
alternatives: all the land ... all the inhabitants of the land
decisions.reason: The word can mean "earth" or "land". Verses 2-3 speak of everything on the face of the ground, and 3:8 repeats "all the earth will be consumed" of the nations, so the whole earth is meant. The judgment that falls on Judah is part of the judgment of all the world.

decisions.choice: jealousy (L), jealous anger (B, R); a terrifying one (L), a sudden and terrible end (B), suddenly (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "jealous anger" so that the word is not taken as envy (m2). Balanced gives both senses of the rare word (m3); Readable keeps "suddenly" and leaves the terror to the rest of the verse. |

decisions.choice: "ne pourront les délivrer au jour de la fureur du SEIGNEUR" (L), "… les sauver au jour de la fureur du SEIGNEUR" (B), "… le jour où le SEIGNEUR montrera sa colère" (R), the published Ezekiel 7:19
decisions.reason: Zephaniah's line is that of Ezekiel 7:19; French keeps the published Ezekiel at each level.

decisions.choice: the Spanish wording of Ezekiel 7:19
decisions.reason: "Su plata y su oro no podrán librarlos / salvarlos en el día del furor del SEÑOR" reuses the Spanish of Ezekiel 7:19 at each level.

decisions.choice: "celo" (L, B); "celo ardiente" (R)
decisions.reason: Qin'ah is God's zeal for what is his, not envy; Spanish "celo" says that, where "celos" would suggest jealousy between people.

decisions.choice: "Fedha yao wala dhahabu yao haitaweza kuwaokoa katika siku ya ghadhabu ya BWANA"
decisions.reason: These are the words of Ezekiel 7:19, so the line follows the published Swahili of that verse at each level. "Wivu" for God's jealousy is his zeal for what is his, as elsewhere in the published text.
